headline: GOLD SNAPS 4-SESSION LOSING STREAK, Settles at $4,570 as Iran Deal Reports Blunt Rate-Hike Bets
snippet: Gold closed up $27.20 to $4,570/oz Monday, snapping a four-session losing streak that had erased $180 from its recent peak. Unconfirmed reports of a US-Iran nuclear deal — including sanctions relief and a long-term enrichment freeze — provided the recovery catalyst, partially offsetting CPI-driven rate-hike fears that had hammered the metal nearly 4% over the prior week.

headline: MINRES REBOOTS Bald Hill After 18-Month Care-and-Maintenance Halt — Lithium Crushing Starts June, First Shipment July
snippet: Mineral Resources (ASX: MIN) announced the restart of its 100%-owned Bald Hill lithium operation in Western Australia, with crushing and mining resuming in June and first spodumene concentrate from Port of Esperance expected in Q1 FY2027. Bald Hill was placed on care-and-maintenance in November 2024; management cited a 'significant and sustained' lithium price recovery as the trigger — lithium carbonate in China hit a two-year high of CNY 200,500/t on May 13.

headline: COPPER HITS 2-WEEK LOW at $6.25/Lb Tuesday as China Demand Miss and Equity Selloff Weigh on Industrial Metals
snippet: Copper fell to $6.25/lb ($13,780/t) Tuesday, its lowest in nearly two weeks, as a broader equity selloff fueled risk-off sentiment and fresh Chinese data disappointed. Retail sales and industrial production both missed forecasts, deepening demand concerns in the world's largest copper consumer, while Iran-driven energy inflation continues to push rate-hike expectations higher.

headline: ASX 200 DROPS 1.34%: BHP Sheds 2.7%, Rio Tinto Falls 3.3% as Copper Tumbles and Gold Retreats Monday
snippet: Australia's S&P/ASX 200 fell 115.5 points Monday as profit-taking swept the materials sector: BHP closed at AUD 58.81 (−2.73%) and Rio Tinto at AUD 179.61 (−3.31%). The selloff follows recent multi-year highs for ASX miners and was driven by a retreating copper price alongside gold's inflation-linked decline.

headline: POWER METALLIC Signs 50/50 Saudi Arabia JV With Amaar Mining to Pursue Jabal Sayid Belt Mineral Licenses
snippet: Power Metallic Mines (TSXV: PNPN) has formed a 50/50 joint venture framework with Saudi Arabia's Amaar United Mining to bid on upcoming mineral license auctions in the Jabal Sayid Belt. The initial approved work program carries up to US$10 million in funding — with Amaar contributing $7.5M and Power Metallic $2.5M — as the company leverages its existing Jabal Baudan exploration license to expand its Saudi footprint.

headline: SILVER CRASHED 10% ON ONE CPI PRINT — Why Six Consecutive Supply Deficits Still Anchor the Structural Bull Case
snippet: Silver's violent drop from $88.48 to $77.52 on hotter-than-expected April CPI data illustrates how the metal's dual industrial-monetary demand engine amplifies macro shocks relative to gold. GoldSilver.com's May analysis argues the structural case is unaffected: six consecutive annual supply deficits totaling ~762 million ounces since 2021, with the Silver Institute projecting a 46-million-oz deficit in 2026.

headline: GOLD-SILVER RATIO Still Above Historical Norms — GoldSeek SWOT Flags Catch-Up Potential for Silver
snippet: GoldSeek's weekly Gold SWOT notes silver has outperformed gold by 10% since mid-February despite the May selloff, yet the gold/silver ratio remains elevated versus historical norms. RBC analysts highlight the ratio as a potential re-rating catalyst: at the 2020 peak ratio, silver's implied price would be substantially higher than current levels, suggesting meaningful catch-up potential if monetary demand reasserts.

headline: WHY INSTITUTIONAL FORECASTERS Still See $5,000 GOLD by Year-End Despite May's Near-4% Weekly Drop
snippet: Despite gold's sharpest weekly decline in weeks, ING's Manthey maintains a $5,000/oz year-end target and Metals Focus remains bullish on prices rising 'well above' $5,000. GoldSilver.com argues the structural case — central bank demand near 800 tonnes/year (JP Morgan estimate), persistent de-dollarisation, and US debt exceeding $40 trillion — makes the May CPI pullback a positioning event, not a trend reversal.

headline: MICHAEL OLIVER: Silver Resilient Despite Iran Headwinds — Sees Pullback as Setup, Not Reversal
snippet: Technical analyst Michael Oliver, speaking on the Money Metals podcast (May 15), argues silver's pullback from record highs is consistent with a broader bull market structure and that Iran-related macro noise is obscuring persistent institutional accumulation. He identifies key support levels holding despite the CPI shock and maintains his bullish long-term outlook for the metal.

headline: ENERGY STORAGE BOOM Lifts Lithium Demand to 31% of Global Supply in 2026 — Up From 23% Just One Year Ago
snippet: Battery energy storage systems are reshaping lithium demand faster than the market anticipated: grid storage will account for 31% of total lithium carbonate equivalent consumption in 2026, up from 23% in 2025, with that segment growing 55% year-on-year (BloombergNEF data). The demand shift is providing structural support for the lithium price recovery that triggered MinRes's Bald Hill restart decision.

headline: NdPr OXIDE FELL 21% IN APRIL to $99.61/kg — Trump-Xi Summit Puts Rare Earth Supply Chains Back at the Table
snippet: Neodymium-praseodymium oxide fell 21% in April — its sharpest monthly decline since Q1's rally — to $99.61/kg as China's VAT policy adjustments and demand uncertainty weighed. However, May's Trump-Xi summit placed rare earth supply chains at the centre of US-China strategic talks, potentially supporting a price floor as Western magnet producers scramble to diversify feedstock away from Chinese control.
